take_homes: What I tell the model first changes every later answer, so context is how I steer it.
The agent goes easy on its own work. I check its report against what I know, and ask a fresh reader for a second opinion.
I save what worked as a rules file, review it after each round, and it improves, like a team retro.

monday.move: Ask one HR partner what in our weekly people-metrics summary is generic, and write my own context file for it. I won't put any employee data into the tool.
monday.who: me and one HR business partner
monday.stop_condition: If the file needs employee-level data, I stop until the DPO and the works council have been asked.
monday.blocker: I haven't asked the works council or the DPO about employee data in an AI tool.

misconception.why: The module never touched headcount or roles. It was all about my own site and rules files. I still think roles go first, and nothing here gave me an answer for the leadership team.

one_line: The dinner-and-context example is good and the habit of checking the agent's own report is useful, but the repeated filler notes were irritating and it never said what this means for people.
